sonar-podstawy.title: What sonar measures and how the beam works
sonar-podstawy.lead: Sonar measures the time and strength of returning sound pulses. The screen is a history of successive pings, not a photograph of the bottom.
sections: Beam footprint

Wide covers more bottom and finds changes quickly, but can combine echoes from different depths. Narrow isolates a smaller target. The displayed depth is tied to a strong return; an object within the cone need not be directly below its centre. Footprint grows with beam angle and depth.
Time, not distance
The horizontal axis is time. Stopping the bait boat or retrieve can make a sloping bottom appear flat. Move steadily and compare the scan with GPS or bathymetry; one line is not a map.
Frequency

Available beams and frequencies depend on the device. A higher frequency and narrower cone usually reveal more detail within their useful range; use Wide for reconnaissance. Do not apply CHIRP+ 2 beam angles to another model.
Your CHIRP+ 2

Wide 100 kHz / 47° covers the most area, Mid 240 kHz / 20° checks a transition, and Narrow 675 kHz / 7° isolates a small spot. At 10 m, Wide covers much more bottom than Narrow. Do not read the horizontal axis as metres.

sonar-dno.title: Bottom hardness: the return and second echo
sonar-dno.lead: A stronger, brighter and often thicker return may indicate firmer material. A second echo strengthens that clue. Palette and settings also change its appearance.
sections: Compare like with like

Scan the same area with comparable sensitivity and beam. A strong band or second return can mean firm bottom, but stone, clay and gravel can look similar. A weak, thin or diffuse return may indicate soft sediment. Check again with Narrow, then feel with a lead: a sharp tap or scrape versus a dull drop and sediment on the lead.
Common traps

Colour has no universal legend: Classic, Day and Night palettes render returns differently. Excess sensitivity amplifies noise; too little hides subtle transitions. Wide can combine both sides of an edge. Sonar alone cannot tell whether silt is fertile or oxygen-poor.
Fish Deeper comparison
Use Raw, the same palette and sensitivity, and scan across the change with Wide followed by Mid or Narrow. Relative echo strength matters; colour without settings does not identify the material.

sonar-materialy.title: Gravel, sand, clay, stones and silt
sonar-materialy.lead: Sonar shows acoustic differences and shape. Assign a material label only after checking it by another method.
sections: Firm materials

Gravel and stones can create a strong uneven band and second echo. Sand or clay may look even and also return strongly. A marker or lead can reveal scraping on gravel, a tap on clay or a different resistance on sand. A single large stone is not the same rig location as a broad firm patch.
Soft materials

Silt, deep silt, leaves and debris tend to return more weakly or diffusely. Check how far the lead sinks, smell, plant remains and whether the top layer is clean. An edge beside deep sediment can be easier to fish, although carp can feed in fertile silt.
Food versus easy presentation

Both bare hard patches and softer areas rich in bottom organisms may matter. Echo alone does not measure food. Compare adjacent patches, assess a safe line to land fish and check whether the rig sits above sediment.
CHIRP+ 2 transition
Mark the change on your personal map, run along and across it, then verify with a lead. The sonar shows a change in echoes, not the chemical makeup of sediment.

sonar-struktury.title: Structure: look beyond the top of a hump
sonar-struktury.lead: A hump, shelf or channel offers clues. A rig may sit better on a side, transition or base than on the top.
sections: Read a cross-section

Repeat runs across and along the feature. A plateau is an area, a hump rises and falls, a channel falls then rises, and a shelf creates a step. Rule out a change caused by slowing down or using a wide beam.
A, B and C

A: a clean edge or top when fish and presentation are confirmed. B: the base of a drop, side of a hump, shelf or channel entrance where food may collect. C: a quieter hard–soft transition or less obvious side on pressured water. Check oxygen, weed and a safe route for landing fish at each.
Scan the feature
Boat or Bait Boat Mode with GPS helps compare parallel runs. From shore, Onshore GPS maps successive casts. Mark the edge and check that fish can be landed safely.

sonar-polozenie.title: Where to place a rig: benefits and costs
sonar-polozenie.lead: Do not search for one magic depth. Identify several safe locations and decide what observation would change your plan.
sections: Top, upper edge and side

A plateau top can be clean and easy to fish but heavily targeted. An upper edge links shallow and deep water, yet a rig must not slide down the slope. A less obvious side may offer cover from wind or disturbance.
Base, channel and transition

The base of a drop or channel entrance may collect food, but check sediment depth and oxygen. A bottom transition or outer weed edge joins habitats. A clean hole is useful only if large enough for repeatable placement and safe landing.
Less obvious routes

A submerged point, island margin, channel through weed or bay entrance may be a route, but fish movement needs observation. Put a rig on a checked patch along the route, not directly beneath a single sonar arch.
CHIRP+ 2 workflow
Compare Wide reconnaissance with Mid or Narrow over a specific target. Save the position in your personal Fish Deeper map and assess a safe landing route. An algorithm cannot choose the spot for you.

sonar-potwierdzenie.title: Sonar + lead + observation + map
sonar-potwierdzenie.lead: Four complementary checks reduce mistakes from one image.
sections: Procedure

Sonar finds depth, edges, echo strength and weed. The map shows whether a change is an area and where it runs. A lead or marker checks firmness, silt and weed height along the same track where permitted. Watch for rolling fish, disturbed silt, margin activity and wind.
Accuracy

A waypoint is the sonar position with GPS and beam-footprint uncertainty. Do not assume centimetre accuracy or that a screen arch pinpoints where a rig will land. Repeat the run and check the actual descent and line position.
CHIRP+ 2 comparison
Keep beam, palette and sensitivity the same when comparing runs. Then use a lead to distinguish firm, soft and weedy bottom.

sonar-zielsko.title: Weed: height, density and clear openings
sonar-zielsko.lead: Plants can echo above the bottom, but not every vertical mark is weed. Compare several passes and check what comes back on the lead.
sections: Low and tall weed

Low weed appears as an uneven band near bottom; tall weed occupies more of the water column. Dense beds obscure the bottom and sparse growth leaves gaps. A clear hole or corridor should recur on several tracks, not just one screen line.
Edges

An outer edge can combine cover and open water; an inner margin may be warmer or calmer. The clear side is easier for rig presentation. Always assess the route to land a fish; an echo among dense weed alone does not make a safe spot.
False positives and model limits
Baitfish, branches and noise can resemble weed. Sonar cannot reliably name a plant species. Vegetation mapping advertised for CHIRP+ 4 has algorithmic limits and is not a CHIRP+ 2 feature.
Your CHIRP+ 2
In Raw compare returns rising above bottom. Then verify a clear opening with a cast or lead. CHIRP+ 2 does not provide CHIRP+ 4 vegetation mapping.

sonar-czyste-oczko.title: A clear hole or corridor in weed
sonar-czyste-oczko.lead: An opening matters only if the rig can actually land in it and a fish can be landed safely.
sections: Verify size

Scan from two directions, mark boundaries and check with a lead or marker. Allow for GPS error and beam footprint. A small opening may call for precise rig placement and a modest food patch instead of scattering bait.
Alternative
If the hole is too small, try an outer edge or neighbouring clean patch. In dense weed, check the landing route, local rules and rig safety first.
CHIRP+ 2 check
Mid 20° locates an edge; Narrow 7° refines a target. Scan again from another angle. On-screen length depends on travel speed.

sonar-ryby.title: Fish arches, lines and shoals
sonar-ryby.lead: An arch can form as a fish moves through the beam relative to the sonar. A line can also be fish. Never identify species from the arch alone.
sections: Movement geometry

As a target enters the cone, passes nearer its centre and exits, its measured distance changes. A partial arch is not automatically a smaller fish. A stationary fish under a stationary sonar may draw a line; travel speed changes mark width. Orientation and sensitivity affect thickness too.
Fish, baitfish and weed

Small fish can form a cloud above bottom; weed grows from bottom and persists on repeat passes. A target tight to bottom is hard to separate. An arch in open water cannot distinguish carp, bream or predator. Compare surface observations and species known to inhabit the water.
Fish Deeper
Turn off Fish Icons, compare Raw and Basic, and repeat the pass. An icon does not confirm carp; one arch does not reliably determine size.

sonar-termoklina.title: Thermocline and oxygen
sonar-termoklina.lead: A sharp temperature gradient in a stratified lake can coincide with oxygen changes. A sonar band is a clue, neither a thermometer nor an oxygen meter.
sections: When to look

After sustained stable summer weather, deeper lakes can stratify. A fine horizontal band may mark a layer boundary, but suspended matter, algae or noise can look similar. Repeat scans at different settings and measure temperature and oxygen at several depths if you have the equipment.
Decision for carp
Do not automatically fish below a visible band or only above it. Cold deep water may lack oxygen. Compare fish activity, weed and edges at plausible depths on this lake.
CHIRP+ 2 limits
CHIRP+ 2 can show a horizontal signal but cannot measure oxygen. Adjust sensitivity, check artefacts and temperature; do not declare a thermocline from one line.

sonar-mapa.title: Unknown water: ten mapping steps
sonar-mapa.lead: Map broad areas first, then refine small spots. Avoid random zigzags.
sections: Steps 1–5

1. Check rules, access and water conditions. 2. Make several regular scan tracks. 3. Find major depth changes. 4. Mark plateaus, drops, channels, island edges and bays. 5. Compare bottom returns at unchanged settings.
Steps 6–10

6. Map weed height and clean openings. 7. Mark hard–soft transitions. 8. Repeat promising tracks with a narrower beam. 9. Save waypoints with a GPS error margin. 10. Check with a lead or marker and fish observation, then select A/B/C with safe landing routes.
Personal maps and Premium
Personal bathymetry comes from your own scans. Global bathymetric maps and offline downloads may require Fish Deeper Premium; coverage varies by lake.

sonar-lodka.title: Bait boat + Deeper
sonar-lodka.lead: A stable mounting and parallel passes matter more than racing around the lake. First confirm that both boat and sonar are permitted.
sections: Run tracks

Mount the sonar vertically and keep it from submerging in waves. Maintain a calm, steady speed, make parallel tracks and one cross-track check. Going too fast separates samples; stopping makes time on the screen a poor proxy for distance.
Return to a target

Save a waypoint with depth, edge, return strength and scan direction. Approach from another direction to confirm shape. GPS and wind add error, so watch the rig descend. Quest or Spark autopilot features do not apply to every boat carrying a Deeper.
Boat and Bait Boat Mode

In Fish Deeper choose Boat Mode for a boat or Bait Boat Mode for a bait boat. Maintain Wi-Fi and a speed under 3 km/h, then compare the GPS track with echoes. Quest or Spark autopilot is not a CHIRP+ 2 feature.

sonar-brzeg.title: Deeper from the bank
sonar-brzeg.lead: Repeat similar casts and retrieve steadily. Changes in speed distort apparent horizontal distances on screen.
sections: Scan

Use a suitable mount and strong line. Cast into a safe area and wait for the sonar to settle. Retrieve smoothly, compare neighbouring overlapping casts and repeat the most interesting section. Avoid snags, boat traffic and restricted areas.
GPS accuracy

Bank mapping needs a model and mode that support GPS; other models may only show current sonar. Previously downloaded Fish Deeper maps may work offline, but GPS still needs a fix. Wind, line bow and cone width reduce spot accuracy.
Onshore GPS
CHIRP+ 2 has its own GNSS (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou and QZSS). In Onshore Mode make overlapping casts and save personal bathymetry. Scan Only without GPS does not record a GPS track.

sonar-ustawienia.title: Deeper CHIRP+ 2 settings in Fish Deeper
sonar-ustawienia.lead: Specific to CHIRP+ 2: three CHIRP beams, Onshore/Boat/Bait Boat modes, Raw/Basic, sensitivity, palettes and GPS.
sections: Starting setup

Choose Onshore, Boat, Bait Boat or Scan Only for the mounting method. Use Wide for rapid reconnaissance and Mid/Narrow for edges, fish close to bottom and hardness. Start at a sensitivity that shows the bottom clearly; reduce it when noise dominates. Do not copy a percentage without accounting for depth, clarity and device.
Screen view

Raw shows more detailed echoes; Basic filters them. Fish Icons are algorithmic classifications. Classic, Day and Night palettes change colour rendering, so yellow cannot always mean gravel. Depth range and shallow-water settings depend on model. Save waypoints and bathymetry with GPS and verify the mapping mode.
Confirmed CHIRP+ 2 specifications

Wide 100 kHz / 47°, Mid 240 kHz / 20°, Narrow 675 kHz / 7°. Target separation: 1 cm on Narrow, 2.4 cm on Mid/Wide. Depth range 0.15–100 m, up to 15 scans/s, stable Wi-Fi up to 120 m. In Fish Deeper begin in Raw with clear sensitivity, then lower it if noise obscures returns.

sonar-raw.title: Raw sonar versus Fish Icons
sonar-raw.lead: An icon is an algorithm's guess, not a confirmed carp. Raw exposes the signal, background and structure for comparison.
sections: False leads

Vertical weed, a branch, baitfish, noise, gas bubbles or a return near bottom may receive a fish icon or look like an arch. A fish only partly within the cone may appear as a line without an icon. Turn icons off, scan again and ask whether the target moves independently of bottom.
Feature availability
Raw/Basic, Fish Icons, palettes and personal bathymetry are covered for Fish Deeper and CHIRP+ 2. AI Fish Detection and vegetation/bottom mapping marketed for CHIRP+ 4 are not CHIRP+ 2 features.

sonar-bledy.title: Common beginner mistakes
sonar-bledy.lead: An interpretation should survive a second scan from another direction. If it does not, do not choose a rig location yet.
sections: Motion and settings

Travelling too fast produces sparse samples; stopping or constantly changing direction breaks the time-to-distance relationship. Too much sensitivity saturates the screen, too little hides fish and subtle transitions. Wide is not a centimetre-precision tool for finding a tiny opening.
Choosing a spot

Not every line is a fish or every arch a carp. Do not focus only on maximum depth or the very top of a feature. Check weed edges and bottom transitions. Never place a rig directly under a fish icon without checking the bottom. Repeat the scan and verify the position.
Check the model
Confirm advice applies to CHIRP+ 2 and the current Fish Deeper app. Global Premium maps are different from your own scans.

sonar-checklista.title: Before placing a rig: scan checklist
sonar-checklista.lead: You need not find perfect bottom, but you do need to know where and how the rig settles.
sections: Field checks

Structure and scan direction; depth; firmness and transitions; weed height and landing route; repeatable fish activity; wind; a second scan; saved waypoint; lead or marker confirmation if safe and permitted; and the rig's actual descent.
Before scanning
Check battery, mount, Wi-Fi and GPS mode in Fish Deeper. Move below 3 km/h. Record palette, beam and sensitivity so future scans are comparable.
